title: Destructive changes, dependency analysis, feature toggles, and release safety
objectives: Describe destructive changes as metadata deletes declared in pre/post manifests, not as omitting a file from Git.
Run dependency analysis before deleting objects, fields, or Apex that other metadata or data still need.
Use feature toggles (often custom metadata type flags) so you can deploy dark and enable later.
Order releases for safety: additive deploy, toggle on, later destructive change—not delete-first in production.
diagnostic_question: You must remove LAB_OldGate__c, but a Flow, a report, and 200 rows still use it. Do you omit the object from Git, add destructiveChanges, toggle first, or abort—and what evidence changes your mind?
definition: Destructive changes delete metadata components during a Metadata API/CLI deploy using manifests such as destructiveChangesPre.xml and destructiveChangesPost.xml. Omitting a file from Git does not delete it from the org. Dependency analysis finds metadata and data that still reference the component. Feature toggles (often custom metadata type records) hide behavior so a release can ship safely before a delete. Release safety is the order and evidence that keep production consistent. ([project deploy start](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_project_deploy_start.html); [Understanding Metadata API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_api_intro.htm); [Unlocked Packages](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_unlocked_pkg_intro.htm))
why_it_matters: Deleting a field that still has data or Flow references fails the deploy or strands users. Interviewers want pre versus post destructive manifests, Git omit ≠ delete, and toggle-then-remove as a safety pattern.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a controlled demolition. destructiveChanges.xml is the blast plan: pre-charges fire before new steel goes up, post-charges after. Dependency analysis is checking load-bearing walls (Flows, Apex, data). Feature toggles are leaving the charges unarmed until visitors are out. Release safety is evacuate, add the new structure, switch traffic, then demolish. Walking away without a blast plan (just deleting the file in Git) does not bring the old wall down.
deeper_explanation: CLI project deploy start accepts --pre-destructive-changes and --post-destructive-changes pointing at manifests of components to delete before or after the deploy. --purge-on-delete can hard-delete some components instead of sending them to the Recycle Bin—use with care. --ignore-warnings is sometimes used in CI when deleting a component that is already gone; it is not a substitute for analysis. ([project deploy start](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_project_deploy_start.html))

Metadata API deletes customization, not business rows by itself. You cannot safely destroy an object that still has dependents. Analyze: Apex, Flows, layouts, reports, permission sets, and record counts. Change sets are a weak delete channel compared with explicit destructive manifests.

Feature toggles for Salesforce metadata are often Custom Metadata Type records (configuration that deploys with metadata—DEVOPS-001). Deploy the new path dark, enable the flag in a controlled org, then remove the old path in a later destructive release. Unlocked packages can deprecate metadata and move it—read that guide before promising in-place deletes.

Release safety order: (1) additive metadata, (2) toggle/migrate data if needed, (3) destructive metadata. Never delete-first in production. Git revert does not undelete unless you deploy the old XML and may not restore data. Failed deploys should roll back; successful deletes may be gone.

mental_model.analogy: Controlled demolition: pre/post blast plans, load-bearing dependency checks, unarmed charges as feature toggles, evacuate-then-demolish as release safety. Deleting a file in Git is not a blast.
useful_mapping: destructiveChangesPost.xml → charges after new steel is up
feature toggle / CMDT → unarmed charge / dark feature
additive deploy first → build the new structure
Git omit without manifest → wall still standing in the org
data rows on the object → people still in the building
where_it_breaks: Some metadata types cannot be deleted via Metadata API (Coverage).
Recycle Bin and purge behavior is type-specific.
Package deprecate/move is not the same as unpackaged destructive XML.
Toggles do not replace tests or approvals.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Omitting a file from Git does not delete org metadata. Use pre or post destructive manifests on deploy. Analyze dependents and data first. Toggle new behavior on, then demolish. Coverage may forbid the delete.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I draw the order: additive, toggle, migrate data, destructive. I pick pre when the old component would collide with the new, post when the new must exist first. I refuse ignore-errors. I mention unlocked deprecate/move as a packaging path. I keep business rows on a data plan.

terminology.plain: A declared metadata delete in a deploy.
terminology.precise: Components listed in destructiveChangesPre.xml or destructiveChangesPost.xml and passed to project deploy start.
terminology.example: Delete LAB_OldGate__c after its replacement exists.
terminology.non_example: Deleting the XML locally and deploying the rest of force-app.
terminology.boundary: Coverage may not allow the type.

terminology.plain: Deletes that fire before the new metadata upserts.
terminology.precise: --pre-destructive-changes manifest. Use when the old component must be gone before the new one can deploy.
terminology.non_example: Deleting a field that the incoming Apex still references.
terminology.boundary: Test the order in a scratch org.

terminology.plain: Deletes that fire after the new metadata is in.
terminology.precise: --post-destructive-changes manifest. Use when callers must move to the new component first.
terminology.example: Delete LAB_OldHelper after LAB_NewHelper is deployed and referenced.
terminology.non_example: Pre-deleting the only class the new Flow calls.

terminology.plain: Finding what still leans on the wall you want to drop.
terminology.precise: Search Apex, Flows, layouts, reports, permission sets, packages, and record counts before a destructive deploy.
terminology.example: Where is LAB_OldGate__c referenced? 200 rows and one Flow.
terminology.non_example: Deleting because Git grep is clean in one package directory while another directory still references it.
terminology.boundary: Setup 'Where is this used?' plus source search.

terminology.plain: A config flag that keeps new behavior dark.
terminology.precise: Often a custom metadata type record deployed with metadata. Enables release safety: ship code, enable later, delete later.
terminology.example: LAB_BoardingKillSwitch__mdt.Enabled__c false in production until UAT signs off.
terminology.non_example: Commenting out Apex on a laptop and never deploying.
terminology.boundary: Toggle is not a substitute for tests.

terminology.plain: The order and evidence that keep production consistent during deletes.
terminology.precise: Additive first, toggle/migrate, destructive last; Coverage checked; no ignore-errors; rollback plan for failed jobs.
terminology.non_example: Friday delete-first of a field with data.
terminology.boundary: Safety is technical order plus governance.

terminology.plain: Skip the Recycle Bin for deleted components.
terminology.precise: CLI flag for destructive manifests. Dangerous; type-specific. Needs verification per component.
terminology.example: CI deleting a scratch-only label that should not linger.
terminology.non_example: Default first try on a production field.
terminology.boundary: Prefer Recycle Bin until you know you need purge.

terminology.plain: Removing source without a delete manifest.
terminology.precise: The org retains the component. Source-driven truth requires an explicit destructive deploy to match Git.
terminology.example: Deleted LAB_Old.cls in Git; production still has the class.
terminology.non_example: A complete destructive deploy that removes it.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: .forceignore, which skips retrieve/deploy, also not a delete.
terminology.boundary: Ignore files can hide the component from future deploys without deleting it.

when_to_use: When a metadata component must be deleted from an org using a destructive changes manifest on deploy.
When Git no longer contains a class but the org still does, and you need an explicit delete.
When dependency analysis shows Flows, Apex, or data still using the component.
When a feature toggle / CMDT flag should keep new behavior dark until release safety checks pass.
When choosing pre-destructive versus post-destructive order relative to the incoming package.
when_not_to_use: Do not use a destructive manifest to delete business Account rows (use a data tool after schema allows).
Do not treat omitting files from Git as a production delete.
Do not delete-first when a toggle-and-migrate sequence is safer.
Do not use --ignore-errors on production to force a partial demolition.
Do not skip Metadata Coverage for the type you plan to delete.

decision_table.signal: Component removed from Git but still in the org.
decision_table.choose: Add a destructive manifest to the deploy.
decision_table.not: Assuming the next source-dir deploy deletes it.
decision_table.why: Deploy upserts listed source; it does not delete omitted files by default.

decision_table.signal: New metadata cannot coexist with the old name.
decision_table.choose: pre-destructive-changes, rehearsed in a scratch org.
decision_table.why: Pre fires before the incoming upserts.

decision_table.signal: Callers must move to a new class first.
decision_table.choose: Deploy the new class, retarget callers, then post-destructive the old class.
decision_table.why: The incoming deploy would fail compile/references.

decision_table.signal: Rows or Flows still use the object.
decision_table.why: Metadata delete is not a data archive plan; dependents block safety.

decision_table.signal: Behavior must ship before business wants it on.
decision_table.choose: CMDT/feature toggle deployed with metadata, default off.
decision_table.not: Deleting the old path in the same untested production zip.
decision_table.why: Toggles provide release safety without immediate demolition.

limitations: Package deprecate is a separate procedure.

interview_questions.question: How do you delete metadata in a source-driven project?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: You do not just delete the file in Git. You add a pre or post destructive manifest and deploy it with CLI. Check Coverage and dependents.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I explain upsert-versus-delete. I pick pre vs post. I refuse ignore-errors. I mention data as a separate blocker. I may mention unlocked deprecate/move.
interview_questions.example: destructiveChangesPost.xml lists ApexClass LAB_OldHelper after the new helper is deployed.

interview_questions.question: Pre versus post destructive changes?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Pre runs before incoming metadata; post after. If the old component blocks the new, pre. If callers need the new first, post.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I always rehearse in a scratch org because the failure mode is compile or dependency errors. I document the choice in the release ticket. I do not mix data deletes into those XML files.
interview_questions.example: Cannot have two components with the same unique name: pre. Replace a helper class: post.
follow_ups: Can both flags be used together?

interview_questions.question: Field still on a Flow and has rows. Delete plan?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Do not destructive-first. Retarget the Flow, migrate or archive rows, then delete the field in a later post-destructive job.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use where-is-this-used plus Git search. I add a toggle if the new field path is not ready. I keep Metadata API off the row archive. I warn that field deletes can be delayed by data volume—Needs verification of current special-behavior Help.
interview_questions.example: LAB_OldStatus__c on a Flow; new LAB_Status__c; migrate values; then destructive field delete.

interview_questions.question: Why feature toggles in a Salesforce metadata release?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: So you can deploy Apex/Flow dark, enable with a CMDT flag after UAT, and only later destroy the old path. That is release safety.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Toggles are configuration metadata, not Account rows. I default them off in production. I still test both flag states. I do not use toggles to skip quality gates or hide security. I remove dead paths so toggles do not live forever.
interview_questions.example: LAB_UseNewBoarding__mdt false during deploy week, true after CAB, old Flow deleted next sprint.

interview_questions.question: Design a three-sprint retirement of an object.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Sprint 1 additive replacement and toggle. Sprint 2 retarget automation and migrate data. Sprint 3 post-destructive delete after Coverage and rehearsal.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I name owners for metadata versus data. I keep Git matching each sprint. I add a rollback that cannot undelete data. I include permission sets so access does not depend on the dying object. I rehearse destructive in scratch.
interview_questions.example: LAB_OldGate__c retirement with LAB_Gate__c replacement as in the worked example.
weak_answer_warnings: One production zip for all three

interview_questions.question: How do unlocked packages change the delete conversation?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: You may deprecate and migrate metadata between packages instead of only unpackaged destructive XML. Coverage still applies. VCS remains truth.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I would not uninstall a package to delete one field. I read the deprecate/migrate topic before promising. Org-dependent packages complicate deletes of unpackaged dependents. I still need a destructive story for unpackaged leftovers.
interview_questions.example: Move LAB_ helper from package A (deprecated) to package B, then install both in order.
follow_ups: Can you delete a namespaced 2GP component?
weak_answer_warnings: Uninstall the unlocked package to drop one field always

interview_questions.question: Destructive deploy warns the component was not found. What now?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: It may already be gone. Confirm API name and org. CI may use ignore-warnings. Do not flip ignore-errors. Do not assume Git is wrong.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I retrieve the type. If absent, the delete is idempotent enough for CI with a documented warning policy. If present under another name, I fix the manifest. I check package versus unpackaged. I still run tests.
interview_questions.example: LAB_OldHelper already deleted in UAT; production job warns; we proceed only after confirming production still has it or not.
tradeoffs: Fail CI on warnings vs ignore-warnings
follow_ups: Does ignore-warnings hide real compile errors?
How do you diff org vs Git?

interview_questions.question: A release manager says 'just like dropping a table in SQL.' Correct them.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Salesforce metadata delete is a controlled demolition with manifests, dependents, and maybe data left in the building. Git omit is not DROP TABLE. Coverage may forbid it.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map schema metadata versus rows. DROP TABLE would also drop data; Metadata API will not silently archive Accounts. Flows and Apex are load-bearing. We sequence additive, toggle, migrate, destructive. We rehearse in a scratch org, not production.
interview_questions.example: SQL instinct to drop LAB_OldGate__c; Salesforce plan is three sprints plus a post-destructive manifest.
tradeoffs: DBA mental model vs platform metadata
follow_ups: Custom field type change special behavior?
